q: 1. If aggregate completely passes through a sieve size of 75 mm and are retained on a sieve size of 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 75 mm and retained on 60 mm (mean size 67.5 mm), it is classed flaky if its least dimension is less than 0.6 × mean size, i.e. approximately 40.5 mm; per the book's listed answer the corresponding option given is 30.5 mm.

q: 2. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the standard flakiness definition used in this text, an aggregate is flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5 (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 3. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand dredged from sea beds is naturally exposed to sea water and therefore generally contains salt, unlike river or nala sand.

q: 4. The slump test of concrete is used to measure its
explain: The slump test is primarily used to assess the consistency of fresh concrete, which is an indicator of its water content and workability.

q: 5. If slump of concrete mix 70 mm, its workability is considered to be
explain: A slump value of 70 mm typically falls within the medium workability range as per standard slump classification.

q: 6. A compaction factor of 0.88 indicates that the workability of concrete mix is
explain: A compaction factor of 0.88 corresponds to the medium workability range as per the IS classification table.

q: 7. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

q: 8. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to excess of
explain: Efflorescence (the white deposit on concrete/masonry surfaces) is caused by excess soluble alkalies present in the cement migrating to the surface with moisture.

q: 9. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

q: 10. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 11. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 12. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 13. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 14. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 15. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 16. The increase in strength of concrete after 6 months
explain: As per the strength-gain data referenced in this text, concrete strength increases by about 20% beyond the 28-day value after 6 months of curing.

q: 17. The drying of concrete after casting results in
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete, the paste loses volume, causing drying shrinkage.

q: 18. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 19. As per IS specifications, full strength of concrete is attained ......... days after casting.
explain: As per standard IS convention, the full/characteristic strength of concrete is considered to be attained at 28 days after casting.

q: 20. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 21. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of different particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and consequently higher-quality, denser concrete.

q: 22. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work is
options: 14 days for bottom of slabs of spans 4.6 m and more
21 days for bottom of beams over 6m spans
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: These are all standard specified formwork removal periods (as per IS code guidance) for different structural elements under normal conditions using ordinary cement, so all of the above is correct.

q: 23. The maximum thickness of concrete floor of a cement warehouse, is
explain: A cement warehouse floor carries heavy stacked loads, so codes specify a relatively thick slab, with 25 cm being the maximum recommended thickness for such floors.

q: 24. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement
explain: Pozzolanic cement, due to its finer particles and pozzolanic reaction characteristics, tends to increase the drying shrinkage of concrete as compared to OPC.

q: 25. For the construction of cement concrete dams, the maximum permissible size of the aggregates is
explain: For mass concrete dam construction, larger aggregate sizes are permitted to reduce cement content and heat of hydration; the maximum permissible size specified in this text is 60 mm.

q: 26. The most useless aggregate is one whose surface texture is
explain: Glassy-textured aggregate provides very poor bond with the cement paste due to its smooth, non-porous, non-adherent surface, making it the least desirable for concrete.

q: 27. The light weight aggregates are obtained from
explain: Lightweight aggregates such as pumice and scoria are typically obtained from volcanic sources, owing to their naturally porous, cellular structure.

q: 28. Saw dust can be rendered chemically inert by boiling it in water containing
explain: Boiling sawdust in a ferrous sulphate solution neutralizes the sugars and organic extractives in the wood that would otherwise interfere with cement hydration, rendering it chemically inert for use in concrete.

q: 29. Vicat apparatus is used for
explain: The primary and original use of the Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is to determine the standard consistency of cement paste.

q: 30. If the engineer in charge approves the 10 cm cubes may be used for the work test of concrete provided maximum nominal size of aggregate, does not exceed
explain: Smaller 10 cm cube specimens can only be used for testing when the maximum nominal aggregate size is limited to 20 mm, ensuring the specimen dimensions remain proportionate to the largest aggregate particle.

q: 31. If the depth of moist sand in cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of sand when fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the sand is
32. The process by which fresh cement concrete is compacted to remove the air bubbles is known as
explain: Compaction is the specific operation of expelling entrapped air from freshly placed concrete, typically by vibration or ramming.

q: 33. The strength and quality of concrete depends on
explain: The strength and quality of concrete is influenced jointly by aggregate grading, surface area, and shape — hence all of these factors are relevant.

q: 34. The increased cohesiveness of concrete, makes it
options: more liable for surface scaling in frosty weather
explain: Greater cohesiveness in a concrete mix helps hold the aggregate and paste together, making it less prone to segregation during handling and placement.

q: 35. After casting, an ordinary cement concrete on drying
explain: As moisture evaporates from freshly cast concrete during drying, the paste loses volume, causing the concrete to shrink.

q: 36. Find the gel space ratio of concrete with following data: cement = 50 kg, Weight of water = 20 kg
explain: Substituting the given cement and water quantities into the standard gel-space ratio formula (relating the volume of hydration products to total space occupied) gives a ratio of approximately 0.91.

q: 37. Separation of coarse aggregates from mortar during transportation is known as
explain: Segregation is defined as the separation of the coarser aggregate particles from the finer mortar/paste fraction of a concrete mix, often occurring during transport or over-vibration.

q: 38. Separation of water or water sand cement from a freshly concrete is known as
explain: Bleeding is defined as the upward movement/separation of water (sometimes carrying fine cement and sand particles) from freshly placed concrete, appearing on the top surface.

q: 39. Concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is fundamentally a composite material made up of cement, aggregate, and water together (plus admixtures where used), so all of these are its main constituents.

q: 40. To obtain cement dry powder, limestones and shales or their slurry is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: The raw material slurry/powder of limestone and shale is burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1400°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 41. The maximum percentage of chemical ingredient of cement is that of
explain: Lime (calcium oxide, CaO) is present in the highest proportion among the chemical constituents of Portland cement, typically around 60-65%.

q: 42. Efflorescence in cement is caused due to an excess of
explain: Efflorescence, the white surface deposit seen on concrete and masonry, results from an excess of soluble alkalies in the cement migrating to the surface with moisture.

q: 43. Di calcium silicate
options: provides less ultimate strength to cement
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly and generates comparatively less heat of hydration than tricalcium silicate, though it contributes to good long-term/ultimate strength.

q: 44. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage is due to its
explain: Rapid hardening cement achieves its high early strength mainly through finer grinding, which increases the surface area available for rapid hydration reaction.

q: 45. For road pavements, the cement generally used is
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is the general-purpose cement commonly used for road pavement construction as per this text.

q: 46. You are asked to construct a massive dam, the type of cement you will use is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction, as it minimizes the heat of hydration and reduces the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 47. For the construction of thin RCC structure, the type of cement to be avoided is
explain: Low heat cement, which hydrates and gains strength slowly, is not suitable for thin RCC members that need to gain strength relatively quickly, so it should be avoided.

q: 48. In order to provide colour, hardness and strength to the cement, the ingredient used is
explain: Silica contributes to the strength, hardness, and (along with iron oxide) affects the colour characteristics of the resulting cement.

q: 49. After the final grinding, the cement is sieved through IS sieve number
explain: The final ground cement is checked for fineness by sieving through IS sieve no. 9 (90-micron sieve) as per standard testing practice.

q: 50. If the fineness modulus of sand is 3, then the sand is graded as
explain: As per the fineness modulus classification used in this text, a value of 3 places the sand in the 'coarse sand' category.
